title: Cohort Guardian: adaptive, metric-aware canary controller for config/model flips
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a controller that runs lightweight semantic + safety checks during canary and A/B exposures and automatically halts or rewinds config/model flips when composite quality deltas exceed adaptive thresholds. This is intended to reduce noisy manual rollbacks, shorten incident MTTR for regressions introduced by model/config changes, and provide explainable evidence for roll decisions.

Scope: controller and small runtime-side agent to collect cohort-level eval signals, an evaluation policy DSL (expressions + weightings), a dashboard for live decisions, and automatic rollback hooks integrated with the rollout engine. We will not change offline eval tooling or the large-scale continuous eval pipeline in this ticket; those remain separate (but will be consumers of the same signal schema).
acceptance_criteria: Controller can subscribe to per-cohort traffic streams and compute rolling aggregates for 5 metrics: semantic-similarity, hallucination-rate, response-latency, token-cost, error-rate
Automatic rollback is triggered when weighted composite score degrades beyond configured band for a cohort for 3 consecutive windows
A/B flows supported: controller records results per-variant and emits action suggestions and a canonical decision (promote/hold/rewind)
Decision provenance is stored (metric deltas, sample traces, relevant eval artifacts) and viewable in Console rollout trace
End-to-end tests demonstrating auto-revert for an injected hallucination spike and for a latency regression
Performance: controller adds <5ms median wall-clock overhead per request for streaming telemetry path and scales to 200k req/s with current autoscaling profiles
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Schema & telemetry hooks (runtime agent): define lightweight signal schema for in-flight traces and per-response labels; add sampling + prefix-caching-safe telemetry emitters
Phase 2: Controller core: implement sliding-window aggregator, composite score function, and DSL parser for policy expressions
Phase 3: Integrations: rollout engine (canary + A/B), Console UI trace surface, and webhook/PR pipeline for human approvals
Phase 4: E2E tests & chaos experiments: simulated regressions for semantic drift, hallucinations, latency degradation
Phase 5: Gradual rollout: start on internal tenant + small subset of customers in Dedicated; monitor and widen
discussion_notes: 2026-02-16 - Asha: Initial design synched with PM/Observability. We want composite scores to be interpretable; prefer linear weighted sum with heuristics for normalization.
2026-02-19 - Riley Chen (Observability): Recommend using exponential moving mean with window=5m and min samples=30 to reduce flapping.
2026-02-22 - Samir Kapoor (Runtime): Runtime emitters can piggyback on existing tracing pipeline; we must ensure KV cache hits do not bias semantic similarity metrics.
2026-02-24 - Design feedback: Console needs a dedicated 'Cohort Guardian' panel showing variant deltas, representative failing samples, and the normalized score curve.
2026-02-27 - Security: telemetry contract requires PII scrub + API key scoping. Security review requested and OK'd to proceed with tokenized sample IDs instead of raw payloads.
testing_plan: Unit: policy DSL parsing and composite scoring edge-cases (NaNs, missing metrics)
Integration: controller + runtime agent in staging with replayed production traffic (sanitized)
E2E: fault-injection test that increases hallucination label by 8x and asserts rollback within 3 windows
Load: scale test at 200k req/s for 15 minutes to validate aggregator autoscaling and memory bounds
Canary: enable for internal org, monitor for 48h, then expand to 5% of selected Dedicated customers
rollout_strategy: Start with a feature flag 'cohort-guardian-enabled' per-tenant
Internal tenant -> bench tenants (redwood-internal) -> opt-in Dedicated customers (5%) -> global ramp
Default policy: conservative thresholds with looser threshold template for low-traffic cohorts to avoid false positives

Human-in-the-loop mode for first two weeks: auto-suggest but require PM/owner approve before rollback; after stable telemetry and low false positive rate, enable fully automatic revert for P0 regressions
monitoring_alerts: Alert: guardian.action_executed when auto-rollback triggers (pager to oncall SRE + channel)
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use interpretable weighted-sum composite instead of black-box classifier to keep decisions explainable for audits
Tradeoff: conservative auto-revert policy reduces customer risk but increases time to detect slow degradations; mitigation: separate long-window drift detector for gradual regressions
We avoid shipping heavy per-request semantic similarity computation in hot path; runtime emits compressed embeddings sampled at 1/50 by default to bound cost
